question.text: Per SEBI's distribution framework for AIFs, if an investor approaches 'Nilgiri Growth AIF' through a SEBI-registered intermediary that is separately charging the investor an advisory or portfolio management fee, how must the investor be on-boarded?

answer.text: Under a Regular Plan with the distributor receiving the normal placement commission.
Via Direct Plan only, which involves no payment of commissions.
Under a negotiated plan with 50% lower commission.
The investor is not permitted to invest in the AIF in such cases.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the SEBI distribution circular, AIFs must ensure that investors who approach the AIF through a SEBI-registered intermediary which is separately charging the investor a fee (advisory fee or PMS fee) are on-boarded VIA DIRECT PLAN ONLY, which involves NO payment of commissions. This prevents double-charging of the investor. The Trap: Regular Plan would mean double charging. 50%-cut is not the rule. Investors are always permitted — only the plan type is constrained. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same direct-plan rule. XXI-B Portfolio Manager and X-A/X-B IA exams test the complementary fiduciary angle — the adviser/PM must not accept AIF distribution commission on top of client fees. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build the 'direct vs regular plan' determination into your LP on-boarding KYC form — a single checkbox asking 'Are you engaging any SEBI-registered intermediary charging you a fee?' flags direct-plan routing automatically.
